payload.claim: When the layer's own branch (no predecessor involved) cannot be fetched, `resolve` wraps `package_phase.ParentGone` as `ValueError(f"layer branch {branch!r} is gone: {gone}")`, but `{gone}` interpolates the original `ParentGone` message, which itself reads `"parent branch {branch} is gone: ..."`. The resulting text calls an arbitrary layer's own branch, which has no predecessor relationship at all, a "parent branch" twice over. `saffron/regate.py:76-83`'s `_fetch` exists precisely to avoid this: its comment says "`fetch_parent_branch`'s own message would call either branch a parent", and it discards the original message rather than embedding it. This hunk does not follow that established convention, so the error text surfaced in the ledger and event log misdescribes the branch.
